Pete Ricketts

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Nebraska · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from Nebraska (incumbent)

Pete Ricketts is a Republican who has served as U.S. Senator from Nebraska since January 2023, when he was appointed to the seat; before that he was Nebraska's governor from 2015 to 2023. He won the 2024 special election for the rest of the term with 62.6% of the vote. He won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary with 81.5% of the vote and is seeking his first full term.

Where Ricketts stands

Taxes
Supports the Republican-backed 'Working Families Tax Cut' law. He says it put money back in Nebraskans' pockets and prevented a $2,400 tax increase.
Tariffs and trade
Supports tariffs as a way to level the playing field with countries that put higher tariffs on American products.
Beef prices and agriculture
Says bringing in more foreign beef would not solve the problem in the long term, and that expanding the U.S. cattle herd is how to lower prices for consumers.
Border security and immigration
Supports more spending on border security and immigration enforcement.
Iran
Says Iran cannot be allowed to get a nuclear weapon and that the U.S. must keep up pressure on the country.
Cost of living
Calls cost of living one of the biggest issues for voters. He links rising grocery and gas prices to the Biden administration.

Background

  • U.S. Senator from Nebraska, appointed January 2023; won the 2024 special election
  • Governor of Nebraska, 2015–2023
  • Born in Nebraska City, Nebraska, August 19, 1964
  • Graduated from Westside High School, Omaha, 1982
  • B.A. in biology
